title: Assistant Manager, Sustainability
description:
Who We Are
  
  
Thriving Weeds Pte Ltd is an innovative local start-up dedicated to driving sustainable change across Singapore. We specialize in sustainability consultancy, waste auditing, data analysis, and sustainability education. By leveraging data, technology, and user education, we partner with our clients—including local farms, shopping malls, office buildings, and more—to embed long-term sustainability practices.
  
  
Our ambitious vision is to rapidly transform Singapore into a sustainable city. We aim to create a comprehensive ecosystem of affordable technologies and solutions that significantly reduce the carbon footprint for future generations.
  
  
In 2024, we embarked on an exciting journey, collaborating with research institutions and institutes of higher learning to develop groundbreaking solutions. Through these partnerships, we are tackling the critical challenges of sustainability and productivity with innovative tech solutions.
  
  
Your Role
  
  
As an Assistant Manager in Sustainability, you will work closely with our founder, Lip Teng, who brings extensive experience in sustainability, waste management, environmental health & safety, and technology. You will support him in sustainability consultancy projects. This role offers a unique opportunity to collaborate with a diverse network of external suppliers, partners, and clients.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
Lead and Manage Projects
  
  
: Implement sustainability programs and initiatives for clients, including consultancy projects, education programs, and waste audits.
  
  
Research & Analysis
  
  
: Conduct market landscape research, analyze government regulations and sustainability data (GHG accounting, waste data, recycling rates), and generate insights for client proposals.
  
  
Presentation & Insights
  
  
: Create compelling presentation slides, insights, and dashboards, or collaborate with external partners to develop these for our clients.
  
  
Client & Stakeholder Management
  
  
: Coordinate with clients, offering professional advice and recommendations to ensure regulatory compliance and reduce carbon footprints.
  
  
**R&D Participation:**  
Engage in research and development of new waste technologies, manage projects, and pilot launches with clients and research institutes.
  
  
**Event Coordination:**  
Organize and coordinate client activities such as workshops, seminars, and trade shows, to drive business development.
  
  
Global Coordination
  
  
: Work with local and overseas suppliers, including potential business travel, to ensure product quality and specifications.
  
  
Administrative Support
  
  
: Handle administrative tasks related to the above responsibilities, including meeting coordination, PO and invoicing, and inventory management.
  
  
Requirements
  
  
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, Sustainability, or Business Management.
  
  
0-2 years of experience in sustainability management or facilities management, with a good understanding of international sustainability standards, trends, and regulations.
  
  
Strong communication skills; confident in working with and coordinating across various stakeholders, including senior executives.
  
  
Excellent multitasking and coordination skills.
  
  
Strong analytical skills, with experience in developing data-driven insights and presentations.
  
  
Passionate about sustainability with a deep commitment to driving positive environmental impact.
  
  
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, or equivalent tools.
  
  
Work Arrangements
  
  
Hybrid (Office, Home, Client Sites)
  
  
What we offer
  
  
Basic salary with sales commission
  
  
On the job training, mentoring and coaching in sustainability consulting and solutions.
  
  
Career progression opportunities
  
  
Why Join Us?
  
  
This is your chance to gain hands-on experience in the sustainability industry and contribute to impactful projects that benefit the community. Join us at Thriving Weeds and be part of a movement that is shaping a sustainable future for Singapore!
  
  
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.
  
  
Thriving Weeds is a Singapore sustainability and technology company that loves turning ideas into action. From working with businesses on real sustainability challenges to experimenting with data, technology and A.I., no two projects are quite the same. You could find yourself working with a logistics operation, a shopping mall, a food business or a school—and seeing first-hand how your work creates an impact.
  
  
We are a small and lean team, which means you won't be hidden behind layers of hierarchy. Your ideas matter, and your work gets seen. We work hard, learn quickly, celebrate the wins and don't take ourselves too seriously. We ask questions, bounce ideas off one another and speak up when we think there is a better way. Our mindset is simple: be better than yesterday—and help each other get there.
  
  
You don't need to be a sustainability expert to join us. We welcome people from different backgrounds who bring curiosity, energy and a willingness to learn. Whether your strength is connecting with people, making things happen, analysing problems or coming up with new ideas, there is room to contribute, try new things and grow
  
  
.
  
  
You'll get hands-on responsibility, direct client exposure and plenty of opportunities to stretch yourself.
  
  
We're building something for the long term, and we want people who are excited to build it with us. If you enjoy meeting people, solving real-world problems, trying something new and occasionally figuring things out as you go, you'll probably enjoy working here. Come as you are, bring your ideas, and let's see what we can build together.

title: Senior Manager, Shared Impact Philanthropy
description:
About ACF and Shared Impact Philanthropy
  
  
Asia Community Foundation (ACF) is the first Asia-wide platform for collaborative and strategic giving. ACF enables donors to pool resources, co-create solutions, and drive positive social and environmental impact across the region. Through donor-advised funds, impact funds, and bespoke giving vehicles, ACF helps philanthropists give with confidence, transparency, and impact.
  
  
ACF has recently launched Shared Impact Philanthropy (ShIP), a new regional offering that will make it easier for funders and nonprofits to work together, providing shared systems, hosting, and operational support so partners can focus on what really matters: driving impact across Asia.
  
  
This is the work of putting good intention into action. Helping to incubate transformative solutions and turn ideas into results. It’s about building what doesn’t yet exist: new systems, new partnerships, new ways of enabling philanthropy to flourish.
  
  
Role Overview
  
  
The Senior Manager, Shared Impact Philanthropy will work closely with the Deputy Executive Director to lead the strategic development and operational delivery of ACF’s platform. This is a senior role with primary ownership of ShIP’s service delivery, platform operations, and partner ecosystem across the region.
  
  
The Senior Manager will manage the delivery of end-to-end project lifecycle of hosted funds and projects, while ensuring consistency, compliance, and continuous improvement across the platform. They will represent ShIP externally with senior funders, partners, and hosted project teams, and will be instrumental in building the platform’s reputation and reach. The Senior Manager will also manage and develop the ShIP team members, providing leadership and direction.
  
  
This role suits a senior professional who combines strategic thinking with operational rigour, and who brings the credibility and relationship depth to represent ACF at the forefront of regional philanthropic infrastructure.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities:**  
1. Strategy and Platform Development
  
  
Support the Dy ED in shaping ShIP’s strategic direction, service models, and growth roadmap.
  
  
Support the design, refinement, and scaling of ShIP’s service offerings, including workflows, delivery frameworks, governance structures, and operational templates.
  
  
Contribute to business development efforts, including developing compelling propositions for new anchor funders and hosted project partners.
  
  
Monitor and evaluate ShIP’s effectiveness and impact, translating learnings into continuous platform improvements and sector knowledge.
  
  
2. Operations and Delivery
  
  
Collaborate with internal teams and external vendors to ensure integrated and responsive service delivery.
  
  
Project manage the end-to-end flow of ShIP funds and projects, ensuring high-quality and consistent service delivery to funders, grantees, and hosted project teams.
  
  
Lead onboarding of new funders, grantees, and hosted project teams, setting the standard for a professional and positive client experience.
  
  
Partner relevant teams to facilitate grant management and hosted project processes, including contracting, due diligence, disbursement, compliance, and reporting.
  
  
Drive continuous improvement of operational workflows, SOPs, policies, and procedures for greater scalability and efficiency.
  
  
3. Financial Management, Documentation, and Compliance
  
  
Oversee budget management, disbursement schedules, and financial reporting across ShIP’s grant and hosted project portfolios.
  
  
Ensure compliance with ACF’s financial, legal, and governance requirements in close coordination with finance and legal teams.
  
  
Maintain accurate and well-organised records across grants and hosted projects to facilitate internal and external audits.
  
  
4. Stakeholder and Partnership Management
  
  
Serve as the senior point of contact for funders, grantees, hosted project teams, and other external stakeholders, managing relationships with professionalism and care.
  
  
Lead the coordination of funder convenings, partner networks, and hosted project Steering Committees.
  
  
Represent ShIP externally at sector events, peer networks, and working groups, building ACF’s profile as a leading regional philanthropic infrastructure provider.
  
  
5. People and Team Leadership
  
  
Oversee recruitment, onboarding, and contracting processes for hosted project teams, in coordination with ACF’s HR and Operations functions.
  
  
Manage and develop ShIP team members, including direct line management of programme staff.
  
  
Provide coaching, mentorship, and performance management to support team effectiveness and professional growth.
  
  
Champion a high-performance, mission-driven team culture aligned with ACF’s values.
  
  
Experience and Skills
  
  
8+ years of relevant experience in grant management, fund management, shared services, fiscal hosting, or related areas, ideally within philanthropy, nonprofit, or international development sectors.
  
  
Demonstrated leadership experience, with a track record of managing teams and building high-performing operations.
  
  
Strong strategic thinking and the ability to contribute meaningfully to platform and organisational development.
  
  
Excellent project management skills with proven ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder workstreams to completion.
  
  
Strong interpersonal and relationship management skills, with the credibility to engage senior funders, partners, and ecosystem actors.
  
  
Excellent written and verbal communication in English; additional Asian language proficiency an advantage.
  
  
Regional or international experience across Asia strongly preferred.
  
  
Attributes
  
  
**Strategic Leadership:** Combines big-picture thinking with operational discipline; able to set direction and drive execution across a complex, multi-partner platform.
  
  
**Operational Excellence:** Highly organised, dependable, and proactive in ensuring seamless and high-quality service delivery.
  
  
**Collaborative:** Builds effective and trusted partnerships across internal teams, funders, partners, and in cross-cultural contexts.
  
  
**Mission-Driven and Values-Led:** Deeply committed to advancing social and environmental impact through collaborative and equitable approaches.
  
  
ACF is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and are an equal opportunity employer, selecting on merit regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, religion, disability, or any other characteristic unrelated to the role.
  
  
Asia Community Foundation's goal is to unlock latent giving within Asia by establishing Donor Advised Funds (DAFs) and providing advice for high to ultra-high-net-worth donors, and matching donor interests to funding opportunities in the Asian region. ACF’s key value proposition would be to help donors give more effectively, efficiently and safely within Asia, by leveraging on a shared infrastructure that is professionally managed, technology-led, and well-networked with the necessary local ground intelligence. ACF is working closely with the relevant government agencies in Singapore to ensure that this entire process is smoothly facilitated.
  
  
ACF’s core offering will be a holistic suite of services from start-to-end to facilitate smooth cross-border giving for donors who intend to pursue an intentional, strategic giving plan. ACF will establish and manage DAFs for high and ultra-high net worth donors. ACF will then facilitate the various steps for high-impact giving within Asia—from conducting due diligence on non-profit organisations, to grant administration and disbursement of funds, and from programme development to monitoring and evaluation. ACF will also be able to provide a range of advisory services and other elective offerings, ranging from education and consulting to recruiting and grantor-grantee engagement.

The **Institute for Business Impact** at Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University, is a new interdisciplinary platform dedicated to advancing research and practical solutions on how business and finance can create, measure, and scale positive societal and environmental impact. The Institute works with partners from academia, industry, government, and civil society to translate rigorous research into business practices, investment decisions, and public policy.

We are looking for a **Research Fellow** to conduct and support applied research at the intersection of business impact, sustainable finance, and public policy. The role will involve developing data-driven research, impact measurement and valuation methodologies, and practitioner-oriented outputs in collaboration with NTU faculty members and external partners.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Design and conduct applied and academic research projects aligned with the Institute’s research areas.
* Collect, manage, and analyse quantitative and qualitative data using appropriate research methods.
* Develop impact measurement frameworks, valuation methodologies, indicators, and analytical tools.
* Prepare academic papers, white papers, policy briefs, industry reports, case studies, and presentations.
* Translate research findings into practical tools, data products, and pilot applications.
* Coordinate collaborations with academic, industry, government, and civil-society partners.
* Support grant applications, project management, stakeholder engagements, workshops, and other Institute activities.

**Job Requirements:**

* A Master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business, Public Policy, Environmental Economics, Sustainability, Data Science, or a closely related discipline.
* Candidates possessing or nearing the completion of a PhD in a relevant field are highly encouraged to apply.
* Knowledge or experience in sustainable finance, impact measurement and valuation, impact investing, corporate sustainability, climate or nature finance, or a related area.
* Strong research, data-management, and analytical skills, with proficiency in software such as Stata, R, Python, or equivalent tools.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate research to academic, policy, and practitioner audiences.
* Strong organisational and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.
* Experience producing practitioner-oriented research, frameworks, data tools, or policy and industry reports would be an advantage.

Work Experience & Skills:

* Minimum of 2 years of professional research or industry-relevant experience, demonstrating strong analytical and empirical capabilities.
* The experience requirement may be adjusted or waived for candidates who possess a completed (or near-completed) PhD and can demonstrate an established track record of high-quality research output.

We regret to inform that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

title: Principal Consultant (Environmental & Social)
description:
**Job Description**  
As a Principal Consultant at ESC, you will play a leadership role supporting high‑quality environmental and planning‑phase consultancy services across Asia. Reporting to senior management, you will provide strategic support for feasibility studies, environmental and social impact assessments (EIA/ESIA/ESHIA), baseline and scoping programmes, permitting strategies and multidisciplinary planning assignments. You will lead teams of consultants and associate consultants, oversee complex and high‑risk projects, guide technical quality, strengthen client relationships and drive business development through proposal leadership, tendering, budgeting and service‑line growth. This role requires strong commercial judgement, sector expertise and the ability to steer teams toward robust, timely and client‑focused outcomes.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic oversight and technical direction across complex planning‑phase projects, ensuring high‑quality, timely and compliant deliverables.
* Lead service areas such as EIA/ESIA/ESHIA, feasibility studies, planning‑phase baseline design, permitting strategies and early‑stage environmental and social advisory.
* Serve as a key client focal point, leading and supporting senior‑level engagements, project shaping and long‑term relationship development.
* Drive business development efforts including proposal development, tender submissions, project budgeting and positioning strategies.
* Manage, mentor and grow teams of consultants and associate consultants, fostering collaboration, technical excellence and professional development.
* Oversee project financial performance, resource planning, risk mitigation and cross‑office coordination.
* Support multi‑disciplinary integration across planning, environmental, social, biodiversity, risk and sustainability functions.
* Champion knowledge sharing, capability building and development of best practices within the function and across ESC.

**Job Requirements**

* Minimum 10–15 years of professional experience in planning phase environmental consulting, including ESIA/EIA/ESHIA, feasibility studies, permitting or related advisory.
* Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, planning or a related discipline; a Master’s degree is an advantage.
* Proven track record in business development, tendering, proposal leadership and project budgeting.
* Strong analytical, strategic planning and project management skills, including leadership of multidisciplinary teams.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage complex, sensitive or high-profile client engagements.
* Strong understanding of regional environmental and planning regulations, impact assessment frameworks and international best practice.
* High level of professional integrity, sound judgement and ability to work effectively across teams and geographies.

**Employment Type:** Full-time

title: Junior Environmental Engineer
description:
### **How you can make your mark**

As a Junior Environmental Engineer, you will play a crucial role in ensuring our projects adhere to environmental regulations and standards. You will be responsible for executing comprehensive environmental monitoring and management plans, providing technical advisory, and ensuring compliance with environmental policies.

**Your responsibilities as a Junior Environmental Engineer:**

* Execute an environmental monitoring and management plan to reduce and mitigate potential negative impacts on the environment.
* Assist in providing technical advisory on environmental policies and standards, ensuring regulatory compliance, and assessing project-specific environmental requirements and specifications.
* Conduct research and technical audits on the environmental impact of projects, analyse data, perform quality control checks, and conduct on-site inspections for instrumentation and monitoring works.
* Collaborate with scientists, engineers, subcontractors, and consultants to develop environmental solutions, and document and maintain plans, requirements, protocols, permits, and standard operating procedures.
* Develop requests for quotations for environmental monitoring scopes, assess environmentally related proposals from potential subcontractors, and contribute to construction risk assessments from an environmental management perspective.

**Your qualities**

You can make your mark as a Junior Environmental Engineer

* Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Marine, Geography, or a related field, with 0 to 3 years of relevant experience in environmental monitoring/management.
* Preferred knowledge of software such as Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, CAD, and GIS; familiarity with programming languages like Python or R is advantageous.
* Full proficiency in English, both written and spoken, is required for effective communication with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and nationalities.
* Organized, analytical, proactive, self-motivated, and a good team player with strong problem-solving and interpersonal skills.
* Ability to work in a dynamic environment with various stakeholders, and flexibility to meet project requirements and deliverables, which may occasionally include weekends and public holidays.

### **We offer**

* Career development: Plenty of opportunities to realize your full potential. Challenge yourself with (online) courses in our Boskalis academy.

**Extra information**

* Your team: You will be part of the Environmental team.
* Where you will work: You will be working in Singapore on-site at the project office of Tuas Terminal Phase 2.
* Fulltime/ part-time job: The position of a junior environmental engineer is a full-time job.

### **About Boskalis**

Working at Boskalis is about creating new horizons and sustainable solutions. In a world where population growth, an increase in global trade, demand for (new) energy, and climate change are driving forces, we challenge you to make your mark in finding innovative and relevant solutions for complex infrastructural and marine projects.

Within a vibrant company culture, you will be working as part of a diverse, international team of experts. We offer you the opportunity to realize your full personal potential and expand your professional career by creating new horizons. Together!

### **Interested?**

**Want to know more?**

We are more than happy to answer your questions about the position, please contact Melisha Nazareth, Corporate Recruiter, via our career page.

**Interested?** Please apply by filling in your details and by uploading your cover letter and CV on our careers site.

**Please note:** Boskalis never requests a financial contribution to arrange visas or other documents related to a job vacancy. Be wary of individuals who pretend to be our recruiters and ask for such contributions.

**Disclaimer for Recruiters and Recruitment Agencies**

We appreciate your interest in our vacancies and understand that your candidate might be enthusiastic about this exciting opportunity. However, our recruitment process is not structured this way; at Boskalis, we handle recruitment ourselves. Therefore, we do not accept unsolicited applications or CVs from recruitment agencies. Any submission will be treated as a direct application.
